annotationRationale: Sign rules reduce the possibilities to two cases. Exhaustive factor-pair enumeration establishes the lower bound, and an explicit triple attains it.
sourceMethod: Followed the official signed-factor enumeration, adding the justification that the positive factor must be at least 5 and organizing all relevant pairs and sums in a table.

review.mathCheck: A positive product permits all-positive factors or two negative factors. The first case has sum at least 3. In the second, positivity requires \(a,b<c\); \(c\le4\) would give product at most 36. The table exhausts all remaining divisors and eligible pairs. Its least positive sum is 3, attained by \(10,-1,-6\), choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA #6 (p.3). It reproduces the signed-factor enumeration and adds an explicit exclusion of positive factors below 5.
review.annotationCheck: The key is correct. Both sign cases, repeated factors and all eligible divisors are covered. The bound and attaining triple establish minimality without advanced knowledge.
